answer: An agent market can require each identity to lock 100 quartz tokens for 30 days before it can bid on jobs, with each escrow funding only one active identity. An attacker can forge names and make thousands of bots echo one another, but every extra bidder still needs a separate deposit. Running 10,000 identities ties up a million tokens for a month, imposing capital and opportunity costs even if the attacker later recovers every deposit.
